title: Invite failure auto-revocation, staged domain verification, and escalation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement automated invite suppression and revocation workflows tied to domain attestation, SSO/SAML signal, and org health scoring. Add audit-log entries with structured decision reasons for every invite lifecycle transition (sent -> accepted -> revoked), and provide a staged domain verification mode (soft-verify -> require-verify -> hard-block). The goal is to reduce compromised onboarding and give SecOps deterministic remediation steps without disrupting high-trust enterprise flows.
acceptance_criteria: New invite lifecycle transitions appear in audit logs with fields: actor, target_email, invite_id, action, reason_code, decision_policy, saml_assertion_id (if present), domain_attestation_status, timestamp
Staged domain verification can be toggled per-org: 'soft' (warning + telemetry), 'enforced' (prevent invites for unverified domains unless override), 'blocked' (deny and auto-revoke).

Automated revocation triggers: domain_revocation_event, stale_invite_after_30d_with_failed_verification, sso_mismatch_detected, admin_compliance_flag -> results in invite invalidation and notification to org admins
Invite throttling by org health score implemented: baseline 100 invites/day; score-driven multiplier adjusts rate and surfaces alerts in Console
Playbook and UI flows documented with examples and rollback steps; end-to-end E2E tests and an audit-log ingestion dashboard are shipping
RBAC v2 checks integrated so only users with 'org.invite.manage' can override enforced/blocked modes
steps: Design event schema for invite audit entries and agree with Observability team
Add staged domain verification flags to Org settings and expose via Console + API
Implement invite decision engine: evaluate SSO binding, domain_attestation, email denylist/allowlist, org_health_score, and RBAC override rules
Wire automatic revoke path: mark invite as revoked, send admin notif, create retention-safe audit record
Create telemetry: Graphs for invites by outcome, revocations by reason, top denied domains
Create migration plan and canary rollout; default to soft mode for existing orgs
decision_log: 2025-01-17: Chose staged verification (soft/enforced/blocked) over a binary verified/unverified to reduce false positives and enable telemetry-driven escalation - decision by Security and PM
2025-01-22: Audit log schema must include saml_assertion_id and policy_version to support forensic analysis - agreed with Observability
2025-01-28: Use org_health_score from Policy Engine as a signal for throttling; fallback to rate-limit configs if score missing
2025-01-30: RBAC v2 integration required so that delegated admins can only perform overrides when entitled; defer UI polish to next cycle
comments: Maya Chen (2025-01-16): Initial spec drafted, adding example log entries and proposed reason_codes.
Arjun Patel (2025-01-18): Engineering spike planned to prototype decision engine; will validate latency impact on invite path.
Sofia Ramirez (PM, 2025-01-20): Add explicit notification copy for admins on auto-revoke and a link to remediation steps.
Design feedback (2025-01-24): Provide two compact Console UX states: 'Verify domain' and 'Override invite' with clear audit trail.
Observability (2025-01-25): Need sample JSON schema for logs; suggested including policy_version and actor_ip for SSO forensic needs.
Arjun Patel (2025-01-29): Spike results - decision engine adds ~8ms median latency; we can batch verification calls to reduce overhead for high-throughput orgs.
Security review note (2025-02-02): KMS policy required for storing SAML artifact references in audit logs; follow up with Infra
notes_for_qa: Simulate SAML assertion mismatch and confirm invite is auto-revoked and audit entry contains saml_assertion_id
Toggle org staged verification modes and validate allowed/blocked flows and corresponding telemetry
Run load test: 10k invite events across 100 orgs and verify decision engine latency percentile and no data loss to audit stream
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal orgs + 5 pilot customers in 'soft' mode
Phase 2: Gradual enable for orgs flagged as high-risk with enforced mode and alerting
Phase 3: Optional blocked mode for customers with compliance needs; provide migration tooling and support
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives may block legitimate onboarding - Mitigation: default to soft mode and provide clear override path with RBAC audit
Risk: Audit log contains sensitive SAML artifacts - Mitigation: store only assertion_id and reference, encrypt logs at rest and restrict access
Risk: Performance impact on invite flow - Mitigation: cache domain attestation and SSO binding results, batch verification calls
